title: LVP vs Laminate: Which Is Better for Sammamish Homes?
meta: LVP vs laminate for Sammamish homes: vinyl plank wins on water and pets, laminate on scratches and looks. Wills Flooring installs both at $2.50 per sq ft.
keywords: LVP vs laminate, vinyl plank vs laminate flooring, laminate or vinyl plank for kitchen, best flooring for dogs and kids, Sammamish WA flooring installation, luxury vinyl plank vs laminate cost

blocks.lead: For most Sammamish households, vinyl plank beats laminate: it is waterproof through the core, quieter under dog paws and kids, and Wills Flooring installs both at the same $2.50 per sq ft, so the extra cost is only in the material.
blocks.detail: Laminate still wins on two things, scratch resistance and how convincingly it imitates real wood. If your main floor is dry, your dogs are big and your budget is tight, laminate is a legitimate answer. If a wet boot, a water bowl or a dishwasher leak is ever going to touch the floor, it is LVP.

blocks.html: The typical Sammamish request sounds like this: a 1990s or 2000s two-story in Klahanie or Trossachs, builder carpet upstairs and worn oak or tile on an open-plan main floor, two kids, a large dog, and a family that wants one continuous floor from the front door through the kitchen to the slider. Both LVP and laminate can do that job for the same labor. Which one holds up depends on how your house actually gets used, so let's get specific.

blocks.text: What each one is made of

items.title: Vinyl through and through
items.text: A printed vinyl design layer under a clear wear layer measured in mils (12 to 22 in good product), on top of a rigid SPC (stone-plastic) or WPC (wood-plastic) core. No wood fiber anywhere, so water cannot swell it. Slightly softer and warmer underfoot than laminate. Most come with an attached pad.

items.title: A wood-fiber board with a photo on top
items.text: A high-density fiberboard core with a printed image and a melamine wear layer rated by AC class (AC3 to AC5). The melamine is extremely hard, which is why laminate resists dog claws so well. The core is compressed wood, so standing water swells the edges permanently. Newer "water-resistant" laminates buy you hours, not days.

a.title: Pick laminate when
items: The whole area is dry: bedrooms, upstairs hall, a dining room away from the kitchen
You have big dogs with claws and want the most scratch-proof surface
You want the deepest, most realistic wood texture on a budget
The HOA or a design-minded buyer will judge the look up close

b.title: Pick LVP when
items: Any water source is in or next to the room
You have a puppy, a senior dog or toddlers
You want one floor through kitchen, mudroom and living space
You want a quieter, warmer floor over a slab or basement

blocks.text: Mistakes we fix on Sammamish estimates

items.html: Buying laminate for the kitchen because it looked better in the store. It does look better. It also swells at the fridge within three years. Put laminate in the rooms that stay dry.
Choosing a 6 mil vinyl plank for a house with a 90 lb dog. Wear layer is the whole spec. A 20 mil plank installs for the same labor and lasts three times as long.
Skipping the pad on laminate. Laminate without a quality underlayment sounds hollow and telegraphs every subfloor dip. Budget for it.
Running a floating floor through the whole main floor with no expansion break. Big open plans in Trossachs and Klahanie need T-molds or an expansion gap plan, or the floor will peak in August.
Assuming both are "cheap" floors. A premium rigid-core LVP or an AC5 laminate can outlast builder-grade hardwood. Read our LVP vs hardwood comparison before deciding it is one or the other.

blocks.title: One Sammamish-specific warning:
blocks.text: South- and west-facing great rooms on the plateau get intense afternoon sun through big sliders. Both floors expand with heat, and dark LVP can get hot enough to soften. We check sun exposure at the estimate and spec a rigid SPC core, a lighter color or a UV-rated product where it matters.

faq.q: Is LVP or laminate better for dogs?
faq.a: It depends on the dog. Big dogs with heavy claws scratch vinyl plank more than laminate, so an AC4 laminate wins in a dry room. Puppies, senior dogs or any accident risk favor LVP, because laminate swells permanently from urine or a tipped water bowl. Most Sammamish families with dogs end up with LVP.

faq.q: Does laminate or vinyl plank cost more to install?
faq.a: At Wills Flooring the installation labor is the same, $2.50 per sq ft with a 500 sq ft minimum and $100 per stair. The difference is in the material and the underlayment. Comparable-quality laminate is usually a little cheaper per box, while rigid-core 20 mil LVP costs more.

faq.q: Can you put laminate in a kitchen?
faq.a: You can, and many people do, but we do not recommend it in Sammamish kitchens. Dishwasher, fridge and sink leaks are common enough that the fiberboard core will eventually meet standing water and swell. If you love the laminate look, use it in adjacent dry rooms and LVP in the kitchen itself.

faq.q: Which one is quieter in a two-story house?
faq.a: Vinyl plank. It is softer and denser, so footsteps and dog nails sound duller than on laminate, which can sound hollow and clicky. Laminate over a good acoustic underlayment closes most of the gap. Either way, upstairs floors over bedrooms benefit from a quality pad.

faq.q: Can LVP and laminate be mixed in the same house?
faq.a: Yes, and it is often the smart answer: LVP in the entry, kitchen, baths and laundry, laminate in bedrooms and the upstairs hall. Choose products with similar color and plank width, and plan the transition at a doorway so the change reads as intentional rather than a patch.

faq.q: How long do LVP and laminate last?
faq.a: Both run 15 to 25 years in a busy household when you buy quality: 20 mil or better for LVP, AC4 or AC5 for laminate. Laminate's lifespan assumes it stays dry; a single flood can end it early. Wills Flooring backs the installation of either with a 1-year workmanship warranty.
